video.title: Why I Give Every Student a Weight to Swing (and why it works)

classification.reason: The coach provides executable drills and cues, including swinging a weight in a horizontal half circle, packing the lats/shoulder blade, and interspersing weighted swings with hitting fed balls.

problem.title_as_question: Why swing a weight to unlock forehand power, and how does it work?
problem.definition: Players often cap their forehand velocity or risk injury because they don't engage their pecs and lats efficiently in a horizontal rotational plane, losing energy at direction change.

quotes.text: This weighted shadow swing exercise is the best way to feel one of the major engines of your forehand power. We intersperse it with hitting the ball.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: It primes your pecs and your lats and your body to accelerate the racket in a way that's really, really efficient.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: So, on the weighted shadow swing, we are accelerating in a horizontal half circle. So, no low to high.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: And what she's doing a lot of this is taking the arm and throwing it using the pecs across the body. Taking the arm and hugging herself.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Now, in order to have this really work for you, you have to use these muscles back here to support the weight as it changes direction.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: And at some point, it's got to change direction and go back forwards. And that's a that's where a lot of injuries happen and it's where a lot of power gets lost.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: What we need to use is we need to pack the lats, pack the shoulder blade down and back using the lats, using the muscles in here and and the side.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: And that gives this soft tissue complex now can kind of catch the arm and shoot it back around.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: the the arm and the weight has something to bounce off of. And it's not like these weak tissues here getting like stretched back and instead it's really strong tissues back here supporting the humorus
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: allowing the brain to be okay with this roll back roll forward action at the shoulder.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: We're going to pick up the racket. It's going to feel super light and whippy. We're going to take that swing a few times.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: And we're trying to feel the same acceleration rhythm, but now, can I time where it releases onto the ball?
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: And when we do this drill, you are much better off missing long and fast than into the net.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: So when she when she drills it a foot into the green, that is a good rep here.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: And I'm tossing these balls so that she can select the height that she feels most explosive and comfortable at.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Can I feel that feeling of having my power uncapped where I can just fire the elbow across, I can rotate, and every time I rotate, it gets faster.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: One of the other things is to especially when I toss it super high, pay attention to what your favorite height is.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: I almost think when I toss it too high, you maybe don't wait a split second long enough. Okay. And swing real quick. And then kind of look, wait, where is my optimal height?
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Long is good.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Now, this pressing exercise and the horizontal swing plane and so many other things we explain with byite-sized little lessons in the digital library.
quotes.speaker: coach

symptoms.description: Capped or insufficient forehand velocity and power.
Lack of efficient feeling of pecs and lats accelerating the racket.
Ball dumping into the net instead of driving fast and deep.

causes.statement: Trying to create low-to-high too early instead of learning pure horizontal plane rotation causes power to be lost.
The player does not throw the arm and elbow across the body horizontally using the pecs.
Muscles in the back fail to support the arm as it changes direction from backswing to forward swing, leaking power and risking injury.
The shoulder complex lacks strong packed muscular engagement behind the humerus, giving the arm nothing solid to bounce off of.

angles.summary: Swinging a weight before hitting is compared to a baseball player warming up with a weighted donut.
The weight primes the body so picking up the tennis racket makes it feel super light and whippy.
Coach visualizes the follow-through as the player hugging herself with the swinging arm.
Coach dispels the need for low-to-high lift when trying to first unlock maximum rotational velocity.

solutions.summary: Execute shadow swings with a hand weight accelerating strictly in a horizontal half circle across the body.
solutions.external_goal: Swing the weight in a horizontal circle from back to front

solutions.summary: Pack the lats and pull the shoulder blade down and back so the arm has a stable muscular base to bounce off of.
Pick up the racket and take a few swings feeling the same whippy acceleration rhythm before transferring to live balls.
When hitting fed balls, check that misses go long and fast past the baseline rather than dumped into the net.
solutions.external_goal: Miss long past the baseline rather than into the net

solutions.summary: Have a partner feed high tosses so you can experiment and wait for the ball to drop into your optimal explosive height.
solutions.external_goal: Hit the tossed ball at your most explosive height
